facts.text: Henderson was founded in August 1852 by Joseph R. Brown, who named the town after his mother's maiden name.
The original Sibley County courthouse, built in 1879, still stands in Henderson and now serves as the Henderson Community Building.
The Sibley County Historical Museum, housed in an 1884 brick house, is on the National Register of Historic Places.
Henderson Public Library, part of the Traverse des Sioux Library Cooperative, serves the town’s residents with a wide range of resources.
By the mid‑1860s, Henderson had two major brickyards—Mattei and Schwartz—that supplied bricks for the town’s early 1900s brick‑style buildings.
The annual Sauerkraut Days celebration, born from Henderson’s agricultural transition, draws visitors to taste local flavors and enjoy community events.
